newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-RELIEVED IRVINE STAYS WITH FERRARI.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-RELIEVED IRVINE STAYS WITH FERRARI.

text.p: Eddie Irvine breathed a sigh of relief on Thursday after Italian Formula One team Ferrari announced that the British racing driver would remain with them for the 1998 season.
Irvine's contract had been up for renewal and the official Ferrari statement came just hours before the team's option on his services expired.
"I'm happy and now I'll be able to concentrate better on the races which lie ahead," Irvine told reporters during a break in testing at this Ferrari track site in central Italy.

The approaching deadline for the Irvine contract sparked widespread media speculation that Ferrari were seeking a possible replacement for the Briton to drive alongside twice world champion Michael Schumacher next year.
The Italian team, which heads this year's constructors' championship, dispelled the rumours with a one paragraph statement.
"The Scuderia Ferrari Marlboro announces they have exercised the existing option with the Grand Prix driver Eddie Irvine in respect of the 1998 sporting season," Ferrari said.
Irvine, in his second season with the Italian giants, has four podium finishes to his name this year and is currently sixth in the drivers' championship.
He plays second fiddle to twice-world champion Schumacher, who leads the 1997 drivers' championship.

"I'll continue to help the team win the world title," Irvine said. "We're always improving and at this point the team is even ready for next season and I'm certain that we'll work even better," he added.
